ai.literal: Duty to do, a person "I will not cease" saying, than the greatness, eminence possessing thing there is not.
ai.translation: There is no glory greater than the greatness of a person who says, "I will not cease from doing my duty."
ai.modern: தன் கடமையைச் செய்து முடிக்க 'நான் ஒருபோதும் ஓயமாட்டேன்' என்று ஒருவன் கூறும் பெருமையை விடச் சிறந்த பெருமை வேறொன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes the supreme value of relentless dedication to one's duty. The word 'கருமம்' refers to the necessary action or duty one must perform to uplift one's family or community. The phrase 'கைதூவேன்' means 'I will not cease' or 'I will not rest my hands', capturing the spirit of tireless effort. The verse declares that there is no glory ('பீடு') that surpasses the greatness of such unwavering commitment.

ai.literal: Manly effort and mature wisdom, thus of the two, by the continuous action, will grow the family.
ai.translation: A family will rise high through the continuous pursuit of two things: tireless effort and mature wisdom.
ai.modern: விடாமுயற்சி, சிறந்த அறிவு என்று சொல்லப்படும் இரண்டின் தொடர்ச்சியான செயல்பாட்டால் ஒருவனுடைய குடி உயர்வடையும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet identifies the two essential qualities needed to uplift one's family: relentless effort ('ஆள்வினை') and mature wisdom ('ஆன்ற அறிவு'). The phrase 'நீள்வினை' emphasizes that the application of these two traits must be continuous and far-reaching, rather than a temporary burst of energy. When a person combines deep knowledge with sustained hard work, their family or lineage ('குடி') will naturally grow and prosper ('நீளும்').

ai.literal: Family 'I will uplift' who says to a person, divine power waist-cloth having tied itself will step forward.
ai.translation: When a person resolves, 'I will uplift my family,' the divine power itself will gird its loins and step forward to help.
ai.modern: என் குடியை நான் உயர்த்துவேன் என்று உறுதிகொண்டு செயல்படும் ஒருவனுக்கு, தெய்வமே தன் ஆடையை வரிந்துகட்டிக்கொண்டு முன்வந்து உதவும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the powerful support available to someone dedicated to their family's welfare. The phrase 'குடி செய்வல்' means 'I will uplift my family,' showing strong personal resolve. In response to such determination, 'தெய்வம்' (divine power or fate) does not merely watch but actively assists. The vivid idiom 'மடி தற்று' (girding the waist-cloth) portrays the divine power rolling up its sleeves, ready for hard work. Thus, the couplet teaches that unwavering commitment to one's lineage naturally attracts powerful, unforeseen assistance.

ai.literal: Without planning, by itself completion will happen, their own family (obj.) without slackening to those who strive.
ai.translation: Success will come on its own, even without prior planning, to those who strive tirelessly to uplift their family.
ai.modern: தம் குடியை உயர்த்துவதற்குச் சோர்வில்லாமல் தொடர்ந்து முயற்சி செய்பவர்களுக்கு, அவர்கள் முன்கூட்டியே திட்டமிடாமலேயே வெற்றி தானாகவே வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of relentless effort in elevating one's family or lineage. The phrase 'தாழாது உஞற்றுபவர்க்கு' refers to those who strive continuously without any slackening or delay. For such dedicated individuals, the text says that 'முடிவு' (completion or success) will happen 'தானே' (by itself). Even if they proceed 'சூழாமல்' (without extensive deliberation or planning), their sheer persistent effort will naturally bring about the desired successful outcome.

ai.literal: Fault being without, family having promoted, him who lives, as kindred will surround the world.
ai.translation: The world will surround as its own kindred the man who lives without fault and elevates his family.
ai.modern: எந்தக் குற்றமும் இல்லாதவனாய், தன் குடியை உயர்த்தி வாழ்கின்றவனை, இந்த உலகத்தார் தங்கள் சுற்றமாக ஏற்றுச் சூழ்ந்து கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the social reward for a person who leads a blameless life while working to uplift their family. The phrase 'குடி செய்து' (kuṭi ceytu) literally means 'having done family', which in this context means acting to build up or promote one's lineage. When a person lives without fault ('குற்றம் இலனாய்') and achieves this, the world ('உலகு') does not merely admire them from afar. Instead, it embraces and surrounds ('சுற்றும்') them as if they were its own kindred ('சுற்றமா'). The poetic repetition of the root 'சுற்று' (meaning both 'kindred' and 'to surround') emphasizes the close, familial bond society forms with such noble individuals.

ai.literal: Good capability that which is called to a person oneself born family leadership having made taking.
ai.translation: True capability for a person consists in taking charge of the family into which they were born and making it prosper.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான ஆற்றல் என்பது, தான் பிறந்த குடும்பத்தின் பொறுப்பைத் தானே ஏற்று அதனை உயர்த்துவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet redefines true capability or 'manliness' (ஆண்மை) as the willingness to take responsibility for one's family. The word 'ஆண்மை' appears twice: first meaning general capability or virtue, and second meaning the governance or leadership of the household. By using the phrase 'ஆக்கிக் கொளல்' (assuming or making it one's own), the text emphasizes actively taking charge. Therefore, uplifting the family one is born into is presented as the highest form of personal strength.

ai.literal: Battle-in brave-men like, one's-own-people-among-even those-who-bear upon-indeed burden.
ai.translation: Just as the brunt of a battle falls on the brave, the burden of uplifting a family rests only on those capable of bearing it among their people.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் எப்படி வீரர்கள்தான் முன்நின்று போரைத் தாங்குவார்களோ, அதுபோல ஒரு குடியில் உள்ளவர்களிலும் திறமையுள்ளவர்கள்தான் அக்குடியை உயர்த்தும் பொறுப்பைத் தாங்குவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares the responsibility of uplifting a family to fighting in a battle. In a battlefield, it is the brave warriors who step forward and bear the brunt of the fight. Similarly, even among one's own relatives, the heavy burden of supporting and elevating the family naturally falls upon those who have the capacity and willingness to bear it. The word 'பொறை' (burden) signifies the difficult task of maintaining the family's honor and prosperity.

ai.literal: Family to those who uplift there is not season; laziness having done, honor if considered, it will perish.
ai.translation: There is no set season for those who strive to uplift their family. If they yield to laziness and worry about their personal honor, their family will perish.
ai.modern: தம் குடியை உயர்த்த முயல்வோருக்கு அதற்கான காலம் என்று தனியாக ஒன்றில்லை. அவர்கள் சோம்பல்பட்டுத் தம் தனிப்பட்ட கௌரவத்தைப் பார்த்தால், அவர்கள் குடி அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes that uplifting one's family requires constant effort, regardless of the time or season. The word 'பருவம்' (season) signifies that one cannot wait for favorable conditions to act. If a person gives in to 'மடி' (laziness) or hesitates out of a false sense of 'மானம்' (personal honor or prestige, thinking a task is beneath them), the family's welfare will be destroyed.

ai.literal: Only for suffering / receptacle / alas / family (acc.) / fault / he who shields / body.
ai.translation: Is the body of the man who shields his family from faults merely a receptacle for suffering?
ai.modern: தன் குடும்பத்திற்குக் குற்றம் வராமல் காப்பவனின் உடம்பு, துன்பத்தை மட்டுமே தாங்கும் கொள்கலமோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet reflects on the immense burden borne by one who takes responsibility for their family. The word 'மறைப்பான்' means one who shields or protects the family from faults, blame, or decline. The poet wonders with pity if such a person's body was created merely to be a vessel for endless suffering. It highlights the selfless, often painful sacrifices required to maintain a family's honor and well-being.

ai.literal: Adversity axe when striking down will fall, having approached who props up capable person without family.
ai.translation: A family without a capable person to step in and prop it up will fall when the axe of adversity strikes.
ai.modern: துன்பம் என்னும் கோடரி வெட்டும்போது, அருகில் சென்று தாங்கிப் பிடிக்கும் திறமையுடைய ஆள் இல்லாத குடும்பம் வீழ்ந்து அழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the metaphor of a tree to describe a family facing hard times. 'இடுக்கண்' means adversity, which acts like an axe ('கால்') striking at the family. 'அடுத்து ஊன்றும் நல்லாள்' refers to a capable person who steps close and acts as a prop to support the family. Without such a strong individual to bear the weight, the family ('குடி') will inevitably collapse ('வீழும்') under the blows of misfortune.
